NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE VIII: OUR OWN STORIES, SKILLS AND FUTURE (LCH-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
From the owner's Volume IV concepts (301-400): telling our own stories, who owns a song or a design, research the village asks for, caregivers and builders, seeds that came home, makers and stargazers, terrible singing, newcomers who stay, and an island that belongs to its people.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Families want a memorial for everyone lost across generations, and the story of how the village survived: build it, or tell it.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) wants a memorial wall carved with the names of everyone the village has lost, across all the generations anyone can remember. (friend) says the village should also tell how it survived the bad years, and what it would do differently. What should the village do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: The wall takes a year. Every family comes to add names. Some names have no family left to add them, and (subject) adds them. People come to the wall to sit. It is not a sad place. It is a full one.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) and the elders hold a night of telling: the bad years, the hunger, the storms, what the village did right and what it did wrong. The young people listen closely. Some of it becomes the village's rules for bad years.
